html:
Srivijaya was a Malay Buddhist kingdom based at Palembang on Sumatra that dominated the Strait of Malacca and much of western island Southeast Asia from the 7th to the 11th century.

It enters history in 671, when the Chinese monk Yijing stopped there for six months on his way to India and found a thousand monks studying. The Kedukan Bukit inscription of 682 records a king's victorious expedition. Its wealth came from control of the straits: ships sailing between India and China had to pass, and Srivijaya kept the sea lanes safe and taxed the trade. It sent tribute missions to Tang and then Song China.

It was also a centre of Buddhist learning. It had ties to the Pala kings of Bengal and endowed a monastery at Nalanda. Its royal house was linked by marriage to the Shailendras of Java, builders of Borobudur in Mataram.

Its power broke in 1025, when the Chola navy from South India raided its ports and captured its king. It lived on in a weaker form, its centre moving to Jambi, until the Javanese kingdoms and then Majapahit took over its place. A prince claiming Srivijayan descent later founded the Malacca Sultanate.

Srivijaya was forgotten so thoroughly that scholars only pieced it together in 1918, when the French historian George Cœdès showed that inscriptions and Chinese records described one state. Recent research suggests its power rested more on land than once thought.
sum: Srivijaya was a Malay Buddhist kingdom based at Palembang on Sumatra that dominated the Strait of Malacca and much of western island Southeast Asia from the 7th to the 11th century.
